The full X is not centered because of its intercept. Use the Euclidean unit sphere rather than the coordinate supremum unit sphere, and retain the source's explicit intercept requirement here rather than retroactively imposing it on the generic setup.

The source overlap condition is strict c_pi<pi(X)<1-c_pi almost surely for one positive constant, not a pointwise assertion for every covariate vector. Separately bound the absolute value of each of the two marginal means by the same positive m_Y; the maximum inequality is exactly their conjunction. This requires meaningful finite marginal expectations and does not turn into a conditional MGF bound given covariates, a mean-zero condition on the uncentered outcomes, independence of the two potential outcomes, or a bound on the observed outcome under arbitrary treatment selection without its separate argument.
